evidence.quote: § 870.2220 Adjunctive hemodynamic indicator with decision point.

agora_applications: Medicine, life sciences and public health

summary.short: 21 CFR § 870.2220 classifies an adjunctive hemodynamic indicator with decision point as a Class II (special controls) device. It sets special controls on software validation, algorithm justification, usability, clinical data and labeling for devices that monitor hemodynamic conditions and give notifications at a decision point.
summary.long: Section 870.2220 defines an adjunctive hemodynamic indicator with decision point as a device that identifies and monitors hemodynamic condition(s) of interest and provides notifications at a clinically meaningful decision point, intended for use alongside other monitoring and patient information. Paragraph (b) classifies the device as Class II (special controls) and lists the special controls: (1) software description, verification and validation based on hazard analysis and risk assessment, covering algorithm characterization, sensor hardware impact, sensor data quality controls, mitigation of user error or subsystem failure, and sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative predictive values for pre-specified time windows; (2) scientific justification of the algorithm, validated on an independent data set; (3) a usability assessment of misinterpretation risk; (4) clinical data representative of the intended population, compared with an acceptable reference method, with agreement assessed across the measurement range; and (5) labeling covering sensor data types, warnings, interpretation guidance, key assumptions and a clinical validation summary. The text sets no numeric thresholds, penalties or effective date.

obligations.summary: Software description, verification and validation, based on a comprehensive hazard analysis and risk assessment, must be provided. This covers full characterization of software technical parameters and algorithms, the expected impact of sensor hardware on performance, specified incoming sensor data quality controls, mitigation of user error and subsystem failure, and sensitivity, specificity, PPV and NPV in percentage and number form. The text names no addressee role.
